r: A **gotra** name; Salankayana = **Nandi** / the holy bull
**Bull (Nandi)** – the dynasty was called "**Nandi**" in ancient Andhra
They called themselves his devotees – "regarding the **father as God**"
**Saivism** (Parama Maheswara); later kings also Vaishnava (Parama Bhagavata)
**8**: **3 Prakrit, 5 Sanskrit**; Sanskrit replaced Prakrit as official language from their time
Land grant to Vishnu – first mention of **Vishnu temples** in Andhra; he also issued the Kolleru inscription
Overseas links credited to the **Salankayanas** – Ptolemy's "Salankenoi" held the coast west of the Godavari, and in their period Andhra Buddhism spread to **Burma and Cambodia**
**Madhava Varma II** (Vishnukundin) conquered Vengi from the Salankayanas

1.x: **Order:** **Ikshvakus → Brihatphalayanas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas**. After the Ikshvakus, the land **south of the Krishna** went to the **Pallavas**, the land **north of the Krishna** to the **Brihatphalayanas**.

r: Capital Vijayapuri; ended by the Pallavas
Ikshvaku feudatories (Nagarjunakonda inscription); only known king **Jayavarma**
Rose after Samudragupta's southern campaign (c. **358** CE) weakened the Pallavas
Founded by Kubja Vishnuvardhana at Vengi
The **only** record of the dynasty and the **first copper plate found in Andhra**
In his **10th** regnal year from **Koduru (Kuduru)**, near Ghantasala / Gudur near Machilipatnam
**Panthur** village to eight Brahmins; text **Prakrit**, seal Sanskrit
Issued the **Mattepadu plates**; leaned to **Buddhism** ("meditating at the feet of Samyak-Sambuddha")
Ruled **22** years; Vakataka marriage; caves at Undavalli, Bhairavakonda, Mogalrajapuram (some texts)
Expanded into the Krishna–Godavari region and both sides of Sriparvata; title **Shadabhigna**; queen Paramabhattarika's vihara
**Greatest** ruler; golden age; Vedic revival; conquered the Salankayanas
Son of MV II by a **Vakataka** princess; **Mahakavi**, Parama Saugata
**Ghatikas**; title Satyasraya; defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma
Chikkulla, Tundi, Tummalagudem-2 plates; put down revolts
**Last** ruler; lost to Pulakeshin II, **624** CE

2.x: Some lists place Deva Varma and Madhava Varma III after MV II; numbering differs between historians.

r: Salankayanas (took Vengi); Pallavas (Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma); Anandagotrikas (title **Trikuta-Malayadhipati**, Trikuta = **Kotappakonda**)
Married a daughter of **Prithvisena II** – Khanapur plates, Satara
A **12th**-c. **Bezawada** inscription – he sentenced **his own son** to death after the prince's chariot killed a poor woman's son
Capital for a time after they gained the Krishna region
Near Vengi/Pedavegi, Eluru; capital moved here from Amarapuri
**Madhava Varma II** (also credited to Vikramendra Varma), to check constant **Pallava** invasions
Most historians – **Brahmins** of the Vishnukundina gotra (B.V. Krishna Rao); K. Gopalachari – Agnikula Kshatriyas; N. Venkataramanayya – Brahmins with Kshatriya ways
**Telangana** – Amrabad, **Keesaragutta** (start as **Vakataka** feudatories), Indrapalanagara; the name is linked with **Vinukonda**
Telugu phrase "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**"; issued from Denduluru; edited by **Dr. F. Kielhorn** (Epigraphia Indica IV, No. **25**; Hultzsch edited the volume)
**Lakshmi and conch** symbols; grant to Agnisarma, Easwarasarma
Grant to Paramabhattarika's vihara; **first Sanskrit inscription in Telangana**
Defeated by Maukhari **Ishanavarma**, whose son married his daughter (**Jaunpur** inscription); **killed in the Kalinga war** by **Prithvimula** of the **Ranadurjayas**
**Pulakeshin II** (Badami Chalukya) defeated **Manchana Bhattaraka** at **Kunala (Kolleru)**, **624 CE**
Pulakeshin's brother **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** founded the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**
The bridge between the **Ikshvaku age and the Eastern Chalukyas**, who took over their agrahara system and administration
